title: Choose the visual world (round 3)
question: The re-roll assigned The Pipeline. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: The Pipeline
options.lineage: the data pipeline diagram I draw at work: nodes and one line that carries data through them
options.thesis: A white page built as one unbroken line. Everything I have made sits on it as a node; a pulse travels the line as you scroll, and the node under your cursor opens.
materials: one 4px ink line running the whole page
one blue for the pulse and the open node
regular-weight grotesk at 8–10vw for the statement
options.viewport: Words only: 'I build apps people actually use.' on two lines at 10vw, the line entering from the top edge and threading under the statement to the first node (Zorest, now). One supporting sentence bottom-left, Email me bottom-right. The pulse starts moving the moment the page loads.
options.risk: A line-and-nodes page can read as a roadmap graphic; it must stay mostly type, with the line thin and the nodes plain words.

raised.raise: One unbroken line is the page's spine and a chase light runs it: the pulse is the signature motion.
One dot marks the active step; only one node is open at a time.
Colour lives only on the line and the open node; all text stays achromatic.
Pressing inverts: every control has a hard pressed state, no soft hover glow.
Past roles sit in a lighter tone of ink, embossed without colour; only the current node takes the blue.

options.label: The Changelog
options.lineage: release notes, the page every engineer reads weekly
options.thesis: My career as a changelog: dated entries, newest first, each one a shipped thing, with the version number as the only ornament.
options.viewport: 'I build apps people actually use.' at 8vw, then the first entry: 2025, Zorest, what shipped.
options.risk: Familiar to every developer; the most common shape for an engineer's site after the card grid.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.thesis: The page as dithered windows with marching ants.
options.case: Retro chrome contradicts a minimal modern brief.

options.label: Drum-machine Step Row
options.thesis: Sixteen steps under a chase light.
options.case: Dark panel and candy keys; nothing a hiring manager reads as an engineer.
options.kept: One unbroken line with a chase light running it.

options.label: Orizuru Crane
options.case: Beautiful, but origami is nobody's reading of a software engineer.
options.kept: One dot marks the active step.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.thesis: White page with colour only at hairline edges.
options.case: Light and quiet, but pastel fringes and hairlines are both excluded by the house rules.
options.kept: Colour confined to edges; text stays achromatic.

options.label: Emigre Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Coarse pixel type at poster scale.
options.viewport: A pixel headline over justified columns.
options.case: Pixel type reads as retro, not minimal.
options.kept: One form repeated honestly at several sizes.

options.label: Zoot Handbill
options.thesis: Stacked billing in plum and ochre.
options.case: Cream, two-ink letterpress; the opposite of the brief.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer portfolio everyone ships: white page, name, one line, project cards, skills, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and one sentence, a button, cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other candidate's site.
